fair_value_reason: I rebuilt the blend with the multiples the agents' own base cases use. P/E: 16.5x on ~$4.80 Oct-2027 NTM EPS (consensus ~$5.3-5.5 less ~10-12%) = $79.2, weight 45%; 16.5x is about UBER's own NTM multiple today (16.7x) and, after the citation gate's filings-based rebuild of the peer table, also about the all-peer median (16.6x), so no further AV discount is taken beyond the EPS haircut. EV/EBITDA: 9.2x filings-based NTM peer median on ~$15.0B NTM adj. EBITDA = EV $138.0B, less $7.33B net debt ex-leases ($12.72B debt - $5.39B cash and ST investments, Q2 8-K), plus $8.76B of non-DH investments at carrying value (10-Q), / ~2.02B shares at the horizon = $69.0, weight 25%. FCF: post-SBC NTM FCF ~$11B at today's 7.33% forward post-SBC yield ($12.43B forward FCF, 0.25 x FY26E $10.49B + 0.75 x FY27E $13.08B MarketScreener, less the $2.03B midpoint of the 2026 SBC guide, over a $141.9B market cap = $69.48 x 2.043B) = $150.0B / 2.02B = $74.3, weight 30%. The blend is $75.2, in line with the agents' scenario means ($74.5-77.0) and ~8% above the $69.48 Oct-5 close. Round 3 (AV narrative scenario): the blend above is the no-de-rating value. In the narrative scenario, every leg moves to a de-rated multiple on unchanged fundamentals: P/E 13.32x (core-7 median) x $4.80 = $63.94; EV/EBITDA 7.93x (core-7 median) x $15.0B = $118.95B - $7.33B + $8.76B = $120.38B / 2.02B = $59.59; FCF yield 7.33% x 16.71/13.32 = 9.20%, $11.0B / 9.20% = $119.6B / 2.02B = $59.22; 0.45/0.25/0.30 blend = $61.44. Probability-weighted (15% estimate): 0.85 x $75.2 + 0.15 x $61.44 = $73.14, so $73.1 (estimate). That is ~5.3% above the $69.48 Oct-5 close and in line with the round-3 ladder's mixture mean of ~$73.4.
supervisor_summary: Round 3 (owner's AV question): the round-2 view of 'no re-rating, ~16.5x' under-priced one specific risk. UBER's own history shows a 12-month, sector-wide de-rating while earnings grew: forward P/E -45% and implied forward EPS +28% from Sep-2025 to Oct-2026, with LYFT -55%. Single Tesla headlines are noise; Waymo's are the stickier ones. I add a 15% scenario in which EPS holds on the $4.80 path but the multiple falls to the 13.3x core-7 median ($63.9). Ladder median $74.9 -> $71.1, fair value $75.2 -> $73.1 (~5% upside), sizing.confidence 0.46 -> 0.39, thesis break unchanged at $52.6. This was a modest under-pricing, not a large one: agents 2 and 4 already had ~25% on narrative-heavy bears at ~11x.
key_drivers: Fundamentals are verified (Q2 8-K): GB +22% cc, non-GAAP EPS $0.81 (+35%), adj. EBITDA +33%, TTM FCF $10.1B. The Q3 guide implies +28-35% EPS growth; consensus Oct-2027 NTM EPS is ~$5.3-5.5 (MarketScreener table last updated Feb 2026; stockanalysis FY27 $4.43 is ~2.5% below it) and agents haircut it ~10-14% to ~$4.7-5.0 for AV and DH drag.

On one consistent filings-based NTM basis UBER is 16.7x adjusted P/E against a ~16.6x peer median (core-7 ~13.3x) and 11.3x EV/adj. EBITDA against ~9.2x. It is about fairly valued, so the return has to come from EPS compounding plus buybacks. No re-rating is supported.

AV narrative is a live 12-month multiple risk, not only a post-2028 one. Waymo headlines hit UBER on the day (-9.6% Dec-2024, -5.0% Sep-2025, -4.3% Jul-2026), and the forward P/E fell ~45% over the last 12 months while implied forward EPS rose ~28% (LYFT -55%). The horizon (2027-10-05) is three months before Waymo's own app in Austin/Atlanta (Jan 2028; fleet on Uber through at least May 2028). Round 3 adds a 15% narrative de-rating scenario (13.32x x $4.80 = $63.94).
Delivery Hero (EUR41.50 offer, acceptance ends Nov 5, close 2H27, ~EUR14bn bridge) and the unsized $10B+ AV program add leverage and estimate risk through the horizon.
Insider conviction is verified: CEO $10.0M at $70.96 and COO $5.3M at ~$75.8 open-market buys in September 2026.
